skill.name: ai-video-generation
skill.description: Create AI videos through the inference.sh belt CLI using text prompts, image references, audio, and video inputs.
skill.summary: Generate, edit, upscale, and add audio to AI videos with inference.sh video models.
skill.author: inference-skills

security_audit.summary: The static external-command hits are Markdown fences, inline model identifiers, or example commands rather than Ruby backtick execution. The hardcoded URL hits are documentation links, a rendered image, or placeholder media URLs, but the skill does grant broad belt CLI execution that can send user prompts and media references to external services. No prompt injection or hidden exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Narrow allowed tools to the specific belt subcommands needed, if the platform supports finer permissions. Require user confirmation before login, paid jobs, or media submission.
Add a clear note that prompts, image URLs, audio URLs, and video URLs are processed by inference.sh and its model providers.

remediation.issue: Related skill install commands in examples
remediation.suggestion: Separate optional npx skill installation examples from normal generation workflows and label them as manual, user-initiated actions.

semantic_findings.title: Broad external CLI execution permission
semantic_findings.description: The skill authorizes Bash(belt *) and instructs users to log in and submit video generation jobs through belt. This can send prompts and media references to third-party inference services and may consume account resources.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The frontmatter explicitly permits Bash(belt *) and the quick start runs belt login and belt app run. The behavior is central to the skill, but it is still a real external service execution risk.

content.value_statement: Video teams need fast access to many AI video models without memorizing each provider API. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through inference.sh belt commands for generation, editing, upscaling, and audio workflows.
actual_capabilities: Lists inference.sh video model choices for text-to-video, image-to-video, avatar, lipsync, editing, and utility tasks.
Shows belt CLI commands for running Google Veo, Seedance, HappyHorse, Wan, Grok, OmniHuman, Fabric, PixVerse, and utility apps.
Supports prompt-based video generation with options such as duration, resolution, audio generation, and reference media.
Guides image, audio, and video URL inputs for animation, lipsync, foley sound, upscaling, and clip merging workflows.
Points users to inference.sh documentation for running apps, streaming results, and content pipeline examples.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and an authenticated account before commands can run.
Generated results depend on third-party model availability, pricing, rate limits, and provider policies.
The skill does not verify copyright, likeness rights, consent, or commercial usage rights for submitted media.
Examples use placeholder URLs and prompts that users must replace with valid accessible media.

use_cases.title: Create campaign clips
use_cases.description: Generate short product, social, or brand videos from a written concept and selected model settings.

use_cases.title: Prototype video concepts
use_cases.description: Compare text-to-video and image-to-video models quickly before committing to a production workflow.

use_cases.title: Build avatar media
use_cases.description: Animate portraits, sync speech audio, add sound effects, and upscale final clips for presentation use.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a simple video
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ai-video-generation skill to create a five second video of a calm ocean sunrise. Choose a fast model and explain any account or input requirements before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a product image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this product image URL to create an image-to-video clip with subtle camera movement and clean studio lighting. Recommend a suitable model and duration.

prompt_templates.title: Create a talking avatar
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a talking head video from a portrait URL and an audio URL. Select an avatar or lipsync model and include any privacy checks before submission.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a full video pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a workflow that generates three short clips, adds foley sound, merges them with transitions, and upscales the result. Ask for confirmation before running each paid or external command.

output_examples.input: Create a short launch teaser from a prompt about a new electric bike in a city at night.
output_examples.output: The assistant selects a fast text-to-video model, asks for duration and audio preferences, then prepares a belt command for the confirmed prompt.

output_examples.input: Turn a portrait and narration file into a talking avatar video.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends an avatar or lipsync model, checks that the user has rights to the portrait and voice, then prepares the required media inputs.

output_examples.input: Improve an existing silent product video for a social post.
output_examples.output: The assistant proposes foley sound, optional clip merging, and upscaling steps, with separate confirmation for each external processing command.

best_practices: Confirm account, cost, and privacy expectations before running belt commands.
Use media only when you have rights and consent for the people, voices, brands, and source files involved.
Start with short durations and lower-cost models before producing final high-resolution clips.
anti_patterns: Do not submit private, regulated, or confidential media without explicit approval.
Do not run generated commands that install other skills unless the user asked for that action.
Do not assume model outputs are legally cleared for commercial use without checking provider terms.

faq.question: What does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires the inference.sh belt CLI and a logged-in account that can run the selected video apps.

faq.question: Can it create video from text?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes text-to-video examples for models such as Veo, Seedance, HappyHorse, WAN, and Grok.

faq.question: Can it animate an existing image?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes image-to-video workflows that use image URLs as model inputs.

faq.question: Does it support lipsync or avatars?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse workflows for portrait animation and lipsync tasks.

faq.question: Will it upload my files automatically?
faq.answer: The skill prepares belt commands, but users should confirm before submitting media or URLs to external services.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when the local environment has the required CLI access.
